name: North Tarawa
introduction: North Tarawa is the quieter, less developed half of Tarawa atoll — a string of villages connected mostly by reef flats and causeways rather than paved roads, offering a slower pace than the capital area to its south.
geography: Separated from South Tarawa by a natural channel, North Tarawa retains a more traditional, village-based way of life, with coconut groves, mangroves, and small settlements along the lagoon shore.
practicalNotes: Travel between South and North Tarawa is typically by boat across the channel, or on foot across the reef flat at low tide with a local guide. Plan around tides and confirm transport locally.
